sections.h2: Which Palm Beach County office to call
sections.html:
Match the question to the office. Anything about value, exemptions or caps goes to the Property Appraiser. The amount due and how to pay it belong to the Tax Collector. The Clerk and Comptroller runs the Value Adjustment Board and the tax deed auction.

The Tax Collector mails more than 600,000 property tax bills by November 1, each addressed to whatever the appraiser has on file. If you moved or sold, fix the mailing address with the appraiser. The collector cannot change it.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, caps, the TRIM notice.
  • Tax Collector: bills, payment, installment plan, deferral, certificates.
  • Clerk and Comptroller: appeals board petitions and tax deed sales.

Palm Beach County has about 1,575,726 residents. Owners hold 70.1 percent of homes, and the middle owner-occupied value is $447,300. The appraiser assigns a two-digit code to each taxing municipality, starting with 00 for unincorporated land, and the first digits of the 17-digit parcel control number carry that code. The number printed on your bill therefore tells you which city, if any, taxes your lot. Cities with codes include Boca Raton, Boynton Beach, Delray Beach, Jupiter, Lake Worth Beach, Palm Beach, West Palm Beach and Wellington.

sections.h2: Exemptions listed on the appraiser's chart
sections.html:
More than a dozen exemptions appear on the chart, and a few carry dollar limits that change each year. For 2026 the senior exemption has an income limit of $38,686 in adjusted gross income, and the civilian total and permanent disability and paraplegic or hemiplegic exemptions use $37,712 in gross income. Eligibility looks at the prior year's income.

Selected exemptions and what each one asks for
ExemptionAmountPaperwork or condition
Homestead$25,000, plus a varying second tierResidency as of January 1; second tier needs assessed value of at least $50,000
Widow or widower$5,000Death certificate
Limited income senior$25,000Age 65 or older, annual income statement
Super Senior, Boynton Beach and Delray Beach onlyExempt from that city's levies25 years of ownership, value under $250,000
Disabled veteran, 10 to 90 percent$5,000VA benefits letter
Total and permanent disabled veteranFully exempt, apart from non ad valorem assessmentsVA letters
Disabled first responderFully exempt, apart from non ad valorem assessmentsAgency certificate, two physician letters

Applications close March 1. Military and disabled applicants can start at the county Veteran Services office.

Three things qualify you: the deed is in your name, Florida is your permanent home, and you lived in the house on January 1. Applications are due March 1, and a late filer loses that year's exemption. You can apply online, at a service center or by mail, and approval renews on its own until something changes.

The first $25,000 counts against every levy, schools included. A second slice of up to $25,000 begins once assessed value passes $50,000 and leaves out the school levy. Save Our Homes keeps a homestead's assessment from rising faster than inflation or 3 percent, whichever is lower; the state chart lists 2.7 for 2026.

A rental or second home has a 10 percent cap on every levy except the school board's, and the appraiser says that cap falls away the year after a sale. Tell the appraiser about any change in ownership, marriage, divorce, death or how the home is used.

Bills can be paid from November 1 through March 31. The reward for paying early is 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February, and March carries the full amount.

Delinquency starts April 1. After that date late tax cannot be paid online, and funds must be in the collector's hands by the last working day of the month, because a postmark no longer counts.

The installment plan breaks the bill into four payments, due around June or July, September, December and March. Applications are due April 30, and enrollment for the next cycle opens November 1. Check the collector's current calendar for the exact dates.

sections.h2: When a Palm Beach County home sells
sections.html:
Unpaid tax follows the parcel, so the closing table is where it ends. The title agent reads the bill and deducts any payoff before sending you the proceeds. Agree with the buyer on how the current year's bill is divided, since bills go out in November and closings happen in every month.

The deed carries state stamp tax of seventy cents per hundred dollars everywhere except Miami-Dade, and every signer answers to the state for it, regardless of what the contract says. It is paid at the recording counter along with the page fees set by section 28.24.

The buyer's assessment resets to market value from the next January 1. Your capped savings do not transfer, which explains why a long-time neighbor's bill can differ sharply from a new owner's.

Delinquency moves through fixed stages, and paying at any point before the auction ends the process. The collector holds one certificate sale a year, no sooner than 60 days after delinquency or June 1, whichever comes later. A certificate is a first lien bought by an investor who pays your tax in exchange for a competitive bid rate.

To redeem, pay the delinquent tax, interest, advertising costs and a $6.25 collection fee added to each certificate. Certificates with no bidder go to the county, where interest runs at 18 percent a year.

Two years after delinquency, the certificate holder may file for a tax deed, and the clerk's office conducts the sale. You can redeem until the sale itself. An owner who is behind can still sell, because the closing pays the balance.

Call the appraiser first; the office encourages that conversation, and its records are searchable online. If you still disagree, file with the Value Adjustment Board.

On the appraiser's calendar, mid-September is the end of the window for market value appeals and denied portability claims. A denied exemption has until July 31 or the 30th day after the denial notice. The state taxpayer page also gives a 25-day limit counted from the TRIM mailing. Your own notice has the final word on timing. The Clerk runs the board separately from the appraiser, so ask what the filing fee is before you file.

Look up your parcel and read the exemption line to see what the county has on file. Open the Tax Collector's account to see which years are paid. If anything is open, request a payoff in writing and keep it with your closing papers. Gather the last TRIM notice and the most recent bill so the buyer and title agent see the same numbers you do.

Whether you list the house or sell for cash, the tax steps are the same. The lien travels with the parcel and is paid from the proceeds, so there is no reason to wait for a perfect payoff before you start talking to buyers.

faqs.q: Where does my Palm Beach County tax payment go?
faqs.a: To the Tax Collector, which bills and collects. The Property Appraiser only sets value and exemptions.

faqs.q: Does paying early cut a Palm Beach County bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The discount starts at 4 percent for November and falls a point monthly, ending after February.

faqs.q: Does homestead end when a Palm Beach County home is sold?
faqs.a: The sale ends it for that house. Apply again for your next home, and use portability to bring part of your capped savings along if you buy within three years.

faqs.q: What is the Super Senior exemption?
faqs.a: It exempts a qualifying owner from city levies in Boynton Beach or Delray Beach only. It needs 25 years of ownership and a market value under $250,000 at application.

faqs.q: Which office records a Palm Beach County deed?
faqs.a: The Clerk and Comptroller records it and collects the documentary stamp tax at that time.
